facts.statement: Microtuban is known only from a single partially preserved skeleton lacking the skull, designated as holotype SMNK PAL 6595.
facts.quote: Microtuban is known only from a partially preserved skeleton lacking the skull, holotype SMNK PAL 6595.

facts.statement: The holotype was collected in the early Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 99.6 to 96 million years ago, from the Sannine Formation in Lebanon.
facts.quote: It was acquired from a local fossil dealer by the Staatliches Museum für Naturkunde Karlsruhe and was, as can be deduced from the qualities of the stone matrix, collected in the locality of Hjoûla in a marine layer of the Sannine Formation, dating to the early Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, about 99.6–96 million years ago.

facts.statement: The specimen represents an immature individual whose articulated but broken bones suggest it died from a collision or a predator bite before sinking to the sea bottom.
facts.quote: It represents an immature individual. Many bones are broken but the whole is still articulated. This was explained as being caused by a collision or a bite by a predator, just before or after death, after which the carcass quickly sank to the sea bottom.

facts.statement: Microtuban was named by Ross A. Elgin and Eberhard Frey in 2011, with the type species Microtuban altivolans.
facts.quote: Microtuban was named by Ross A. Elgin and Eberhard Frey in 2011 and the type species is Microtuban altivolans.

facts.statement: The fossil's upper arm measured about nine centimeters and the lower arm about seven centimeters.
facts.quote: The upper arm, damaged in the fossil, measured about nine centimetres, the lower about seven.

facts.statement: The fourth metacarpal of the specimen is 122 millimeters long.
facts.quote: The fourth metacarpal is 122 millimetres long.

facts.statement: Microtuban possesses two unique traits: the second wing-finger phalanx is long at 85% of the first phalanx's length, and the fourth phalanx is extremely reduced at 1.1% of the wing-finger length.
facts.quote: The authors indicated two unique derived traits, or autapomorphies: the second phalanx of the wing-finger is long, with 85% of the length of the first phalanx; the fourth phalanx is extremely reduced measuring but 1.1% of wing-finger length.

facts.statement: Possible juvenile traits in the specimen include the lack of a notarium and unfused scapula and coracoid bones.
facts.quote: Possible juvenile traits included the lack of a notarium, being a fusion of the front dorsal vertebrae, and an unfused scapula and coracoid.

facts.statement: Microtuban was assigned to the Azhdarchoidea superfamily using the comparative method.
facts.quote: The describers assigned Microtuban to the Azhdarchoidea, using the comparative method.

facts.statement: It is impossible to definitively classify Microtuban as a thalassodromid or chaoyangopterid because the distinguishing traits are located in the skull, which is missing from the holotype.
facts.quote: As the two latter groups are mainly distinguished on the basis of traits in the skull, the very body part the Microtuban holotype lacks, it proved impossible to decide whether it were a thalassodromid or a chaoyangopterid.

facts.statement: A 2018 study by Nicholas Longrich and colleagues placed Microtuban within the Chaoyangopteridae at the basalmost position.
facts.quote: A study upheld by paleontologist Nicholas Longrich and colleagues in 2018 had recovered Microtuban within the Chaoyangopteridae, in the basalmost position.

facts.statement: The fourth metacarpal measures 122 millimeters in length.

facts.statement: The four phalanges of the fourth wing finger measure 135, 114.5, 63.5, and 3.5 millimeters respectively.

facts.statement: The authors identified two unique derived traits: the second wing-finger phalanx is long, measuring about 85% of the first phalanx, while the fourth phalanx is extremely reduced at 1.1% of the wing-finger length.
facts.quote: Los autores indicaron dos rasgos únicos derivados, o autapomorfias: la segunda flange del dedo alar es larga, con cerca del 85% de la longitud de la primera falange; la cuarta falange es extremadamente reducida midiendo solo el 1.1% de la longitud del dedo del ala.

facts.statement: The generic name derives from the Greek word for 'small' and the Arabic word for 'dragon' or basilisk, also referring to Thuban, the ancient polar star in the constellation Draco.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del término griego μικρός, mikros, "pequeño", y el árabe التنين, tuban, "dragón" o basilisco, también refiriéndose a Thuban, la antigua estrella polar en la constelación de Draco.

facts.statement: The species name derives from the Latin words for 'high' and 'to fly'.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se deriva del latín altus, "alto", y volare, "volar".

facts.statement: Because both groups are distinguished mainly by skull characteristics, which the Microtuban holotype lacks, it is impossible to prove whether it was a thalassodromid or a chaoyangopterid.
facts.quote: Dado que ambos grupos se distinguen mayormente basándose en características del cráneo, parte de la que el holotipo de Microtuban carece, es imposible probar si era un talasodrómido o un chaoyangoptérido.

facts.statement: Microtuban lived during the Cenomanian stage, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
